request.song: All You Ever Do Is Bring Me Down

original.guitar: The Mavericks (Nick Kane on lead guitar at the time; track credits not found)
original.amp: Not documented. The Mavericks' retro sound: clean Fender-style amps with plenty of spring reverb
original.notes: Single from Music for All Occasions (January 1996), featuring Flaco Jiménez on accordion, who plays the solo.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the clean, bouncy Tex-Mex rhythm: short, choppy strums on the off-beats, polka style, so the accordion and bass carry the downbeats. Channel B for a warmer tweed sound in the louder sections.
recipes.why: The Mavericks' sound mixes Tex-Mex, country and 60s pop: clean Fender amps, a short slapback and plenty of spring reverb. The guitar stays out of the way of the accordion.

request.song: All You Ever Do Is Bring Me Down

original.guitar: The Mavericks (Nick Kane on lead guitar at the time; track credits not found)
original.amp: Not documented. Retro twang: clean Fender-style amp, EL84 for warmer lines
original.effects: Spring reverb, slapback, tremolo (style, not documented)
original.notes: Single from Music for All Occasions (January 1996). The solo is on accordion (Flaco Jiménez).

recipes.tips: Channel A for twangy, Duane Eddy-style lines on the low strings and fills between the vocal lines. Channel B for warmer melody lines. Stomp MOD for a retro tremolo. The solo on the record is accordion: if you cover it on guitar, use channel B and play it with lots of short, picked notes.
recipes.why: Retro twang is a clean Fender with a lot of spring reverb and slapback, picked hard on the bridge pickup. The AC15TB on channel B is a rounder voice for melodies.
